name: Can I keep living in the house during a rear addition?

mainEntity.name: Is it realistic to stay in the home while the rear addition is being built, or should I plan to move out?
mainEntity.text: Is it realistic to stay in the home while the rear addition is being built, or should I plan to move out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Staying in the house during a rear addition is possible for some projects, but it becomes much harder when the work affects the kitchen, bathrooms, exterior access, or major utilities. Homeowners often underestimate the disruption caused by demolition, framing, inspections, and rough-in work. If the rear of the house is being opened up for weeks or months, dust control and daily movement through the home can be challenging. Living on-site can save temporary housing costs, but it may slow the project and reduce comfort. The decision should be made before construction begins, because staging, protection, and access routes all depend on whether the home is occupied. For a luxury remodel, many owners prefer to move out if the addition is extensive, especially when the back half of the home is under construction. A realistic conversation with the builder about phases, shutoffs, and access is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sometimes yes, but it depends on how much of the house is affected. If the rear portion, kitchen, or utilities are heavily disrupted, living on-site can become impractical because of dust, noise, loss of access, and safety concerns.
